tools.name: improve_prompt
tools.description: Rewrite a rough prompt into a sharper, ready-to-use prompt structured as Role, Task, Context, Format (RTCF). Returns the improved prompt, its four parts, a short list of clarifying questions worth asking the user, and which model tier and effort level suit this kind of work. Use this before answerin

tools.name: improve_followup
tools.description: Write the user's NEXT message for an AI conversation that is already in progress (a follow-up). Use when the user wants to refine, deepen, or continue earlier work in this conversation. Do NOT use it for a brand-new task (use improve_prompt for that). Returns a short, ready-to-send continuation mess

tools.name: build_prompt
tools.description: Compose a ready-to-use prompt from explicit Role, Task, Context, and Format parts. Use when the user already knows the pieces and wants them woven into one clean prompt.

findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "improve_prompt" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

evidence.snippet: Rewrite a rough prompt into a sharper, ready-to-use prompt structured as Role, Task, Context, Format (RTCF). Returns the improved prompt, its four parts, a shor…

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "improve_prompt" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
